> the numbered plans in directory listings — call this out as the registry,
> not a plan. Per-plan §3.1 rows are still the preferred home for anchors

> **CI/pre-commit guard** (`scripts/check-anchor-registry/check-anchor-registry.{sh,ps1}`): every
> `D-*` identifier appearing in `src/` MUST resolve to a row in ANY of the three
> registry documents (a closed anchor's row lives in `-done.md`, and a citation of
> it must still resolve)
> OR a citation in any `.plans/*.md`. Pre-fix this recurred TWICE

> The guard makes the system enforce the discipline — same shape as the
> agnosticism veto + the `CallConv` static_assert.
>
> **★ ANCHOR-NAME RULE — READ BEFORE INVENTING A `D-*` NAME (documented 2026-07-28, TF-C81; it was
> load-bearing and unwritten until it bit).** The guard's regex is
> `D-[A-Z0-9_]+(-[A-Z0-9_]+){2,}` — **`D-` plus THREE OR MORE `-`-separated segments is a
> DEFERRED-WORK ANCHOR and MUST resolve to a row here; a TWO-segment `D-*` name (`D-OPT`) is an
> informal feature label the guard ignores.** So hyphenating a COMPOUND FEATURE WORD silently changes
> the identifier's CLASS: `D-CSUBSET-ALWAYS-INLINE` tripped the guard and had to be renamed
> `D-CSUBSET-ALWAYSINLINE` to match its sibling `D-CSUBSET-NOINLINE`. The failure surfaces as
> “missing row”, which misdirects you into WRITING a duplicate row instead of FIXING the name.
> **Spell a compound feature word as ONE segment (`ALWAYSINLINE`, `NOINLINE`); reserve hyphens for
> genuine name components; when in doubt, match the sibling anchor already in this file.** Full
> write-up: [[D-PLANS-ANCHOR-NAME-SEGMENT-COUNT-GATE]].

> **★★ MEASUREMENT CAVEAT — READ BEFORE QUOTING ANY “this will clear N errors” NUMBER IN THIS FILE (2026-07-28, macOS-arm64 predefine-probe cycle).** DSS **abandons a TU at its first hard parse failure**, so a corpus error count is a count of the errors REACHED, never of the defects PRESENT. Clearing an early blocker therefore EXPOSES later ones that were never reached, and a drop in the total is NOT a count of defects fixed. Worked example from this cycle: the 189-TU sqlite build went **213 → 80** total errors when architecture + toolchain predefines were both supplied — that is **NOT 133 defects fixed**; the residual 80 is a NEWLY-EXPOSED population whose composition was unknown until separately measured. It is equally possible for a real fix to make the total go UP (this cycle measured exactly that: toolchain-identity macros ALONE took 213 → 216). Every forward estimate of the form “closing X clears N errors” in any row below MUST be read with this caveat, and every new one MUST carry it. See [[D-MEASURE-FIRST-FAILURE-MASKS-RESIDUAL]] for the citable class row.

> 1555 closed rows: 1114 lifted from `_deferred-anchor-registry-production.md` and 441 from

>
> **★★★ WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (operator, 2026-09-01).** *"split what's done from
> what's to be done. this way we adjust our skills to only read what's yet to be done."*
> The registry's own preamble has always said **never delete a closed row -- the audit
> trail is load-bearing for future regressions**. That is still the rule; this file is
> where the trail now lives. The two working registries became a list of what REMAINS.
>
> ★ **RESOLUTION READS THIS FILE; ORIENTATION MUST NOT.**
> A `D-*` anchor cited in `src/` resolves against every registry document, so
> `check-anchor-registry` and every other RESOLVER globs `_deferred-anchor-registry*.md`
> and finds rows here. But no instrument that answers *what should I work on* may read
> this file: `burndown-queue` excludes it by name, and the cycle's priority pick reads
> production and harness only.
>
> ⚠ **AN OPEN ROW IN THIS FILE IS A REFUSAL.** `check-anchor-balance` fails the tree
> when the partition breaks in either direction -- a closed row left in a working
> registry, or an open row filed here. Reopening a row is a MOVE BACK, performed by
> `scripts/apply-registry-row/apply-registry-row.py`; it is never an edit in place.
>
> ★ **THE ORIGIN BUCKET SURVIVES THE MOVE**, which is why this file carries TWO tables
> rather than one merged list. A reopened row goes back to the registry it came from, and
> *"was this a defect a user could hit?"* stays answerable after the fact. Flattening the
> two would have thrown away the one fact the 2026-08-25 production/harness split exists
> to record.

## Closed — Production

**Row shape: EXACTLY six cells — `Anchor`, `Priority`, `Status`, `Trigger`, `Closing work`, `Cross-refs`.**
★★★ **`Priority` IS `P0`..`P5` AND `Status` IS ONE OF `✅ CLOSED` / `🟠 OPEN` / `⏳ GATED` — a three-value controlled vocabulary, added
2026-09-01 on the operator's instruction: *"add columns for priority and status ... this way
we always have clean statuses."* Before that the verdict was the FIRST GLYPH of a prose blob
that also carried the trigger, the history and the retraction, and every reader had to agree
where the verdict stopped — which is precisely the agreement that failed four times in
`check-anchor-balance`'s own comment history.
⚠ **THE STATUS CELL KEEPS ITS GLYPH, AND THE GLYPH IS THE CONTRACT.** A row is CLOSED iff its
status cell OPENS with ✅ after stripping `*_ ` — the complement defined, never the variants,
so a glyph nobody has thought of yet counts OPEN. A column holding the bare WORD `CLOSED`
would make that test false for every closed row at once. The word is for the reader.
⚠ **`Priority` IS A DECLARATION, NOT A SIEVE RESULT.** `burndown-queue` seeds it and then
READS it; its own docstring warns that a band is *"a sort key, not a verdict"* because a
census built from that keyword sieve reported 103 where the truth was 4. Correct the cell and
the correction survives, which re-running a sieve never does.
★ **DO NOT HAND-WRITE A ROW.** `scripts/anchors/anchors.py` (and its `write-anchor` /
`set-anchor` / `read-anchor` / `read-anchors` launchers) takes the FIELDS and produces the row,
so a wrapped id, an unescaped pipe and a wrong cell count are all inexpressible.
A row with fewer cells shifts every following cell one column LEFT; a row with more
has the surplus SILENTLY DROPPED by the renderer. Neither is visible when reading the
raw text, so the count is load-bearing — see `D-PLANS-REGISTRY-MALFORMED-ROW-CELLS`.

Two authoring rules follow from that, both verified against the GitHub renderer:
- **A raw `|` splits a cell EVEN INSIDE BACKTICKS.** To quote an expression, regex or
  alternation containing one, write `\|` — the backslash-escaped form is the *only*
  one that survives inside a code span (an HTML entity does **not**).
- **` ═══ ` inside a cell marks a seam where two cells were joined** when a row
  authored to a wider schema was converged onto these four columns. It is a joint in
  the prose, not a column boundary.

⚠ **APPEND AT END-OF-TABLE, NEVER AT END-OF-FILE, AND TO THE TABLE THAT MATCHES THE
ROW'S ORIGIN REGISTRY.** The working registries carry exactly one anchor table each,
for a reason this file has to state differently: this registry once had a second
`## Anchor Index (continued)` table that existed only because rows had been appended
past the end of the file, and its header declared TWO columns, so every fuller row
silently lost its `Closing work` and `Cross-refs`. **The two tables HERE are not that
accident** — they are the production/harness bucket, preserved across the move so a
reopened row knows which working list it returns to. Both declare the same four
columns. `scripts/apply-registry-row/apply-registry-row.py` picks the table from the
registry named on its command line; it is the only thing that should be appending here.

SP, the prologue, the unwind data, the spill addressing and the register allocation are then all untouched, which is why this lands with no arch-keyed code, no new opcode, no new config key and no new diagnostic code. MSVC's own answer (an aligned base register) is the same family and strictly heavier: it burns a register and rewrites the prologue. ★ AGNOSTIC BY REUSE, NOT BY DISCIPLINE — THE PRIMITIVE ALREADY EXISTED IN THE FILE. `lowerVlaAlloca` had been rounding a VLA's runtime byte count since D-CSUBSET-VLA with `add reg, A-1` + a materialized NEGATIVE mask + a REG-REG `and`, the single form both shipped ISAs declare (x86_64 also has an AND-imm32; AArch64's logical immediates are a different encoding entirely, so a reg-imm spelling would impose one ISA's shape on the other). It is now `emitAlignUpToPowerOfTwo`, shared by every caller and emitted over VIRTUAL registers pre-regalloc, so 2-address legalization, allocation and the peepholes see three unremarkable arithmetic instructions. THE FRAME HALF is two pure derivations PUBLISHED in `lir_callconv.hpp` beside `frameSlotStride`, for the reason that one is: `frameSlotPlacementAlign` (an alloca's in-frame offset rounds to min(its own alignment, the frame's) — rounding past the base's own guarantee buys nothing) and `frameSlotAlignHeadroom` (`align > frameAlign` gives `align - frameAlign`, else 0). Rules 1–7 are TYPE tests, and the pair that dominates real C — a local array or struct (the shapes Mem2Reg cannot promote, so their Loads survive to CSE/LICM) against a parameter — has IDENTICAL pointee types, so NO type rule can ever separate it. **(3) THE RESOLUTION, DELIVERED EXACTLY AS WRITTEN: "the (def,location)-keyed walk-past layer OVER the existing index — never a per-block stop cache."** `MirMemoryClobbers` builds ONE `MirPointerEscape` per pass and threads it into every probe, and Q1/Q2/Q3 now funnel every def visit through `defClobbers_`, a memo of the UNCHANGED `mirInstClobbersLoadPtr` keyed on (def, location) with the two flags selecting one of four tables, bounded at `kMaxVerdictEntries`, with a fail-loud refusal of a second `TypeInterner` (the key does not carry it). A def whose verdict for THIS location is known is passed over with no alias reasoning — the "structurally skip provably-non-aliasing defs" this row asked for — while nothing stops a walk or truncates an enumeration, which is what keeps the REJECTED frontier design rejected (`FrontierStopsAtNonAliasingStoreMustStillRefuse` still green, plus the new `WalkPastMemoNeverMasksAFartherAliasingClobber` which re-refutes it at the HIGHER precision where a nearer def really does answer No). `aliasTestCount()` / `aliasTestSkipCount()` make this row's OTHER trigger (*"a profile shows the index's per-query alias-TEST count dominating a pass"*) a number tests read rather than a claim. **✔MEASURED (Windows host, `build/lane-f` Debug, parent 57b75813):** full ctest **1685/1688**, and all three reds re-run GREEN in isolation — `stale_refusal_citations_guard` and `program/test_compile_pipeline` were cross-lane/parallel-run transients (a `Permission denied` rename under -j8), `line_endings_guard` was this lane's own CRLF and was fixed. The skip is real: repeating ONE query runs 4 alias tests then 0, with 4 skips, and a DIFFERENT location is tested afresh (the key carries the location). The precision REACHES its consumer — `runCse`, unmodified, now reuses a Load across a Store through a parameter when the slot stayed home (`instructionsCsed` 2) and refuses it when the same slot's address was published to a global (`instructionsCsed` 1). And the shipped `release` image for the new corpus example CHANGES when Rule 3b is disabled (md5 `e47235c5…` vs `7d83c6c8…`, x86_64:pe64, both exit 16), so the example exercises the feature rather than merely running. **RED-ON-DISABLE — three mutants, each md5-proven BUILT and its failure arm EXERCISED, each restored:** (A) Rule 3b removed from `mirMayAlias` (test binaries `02402216…`→`1e548843…` and `f706fef1…`→`c89df119…`) reds `MirAlias.Rule3b_NonEscapingSlotVersusAParameterIsNo`, `MirMemoryClobbers.ParameterStoresDoNotClobberANonEscapedLocalSlot` and the pass-tier CSE pin; (B) the `verdicts_` lookup removed from `defClobbers_` (`c89df119…`→`6ebba3ed…`) reds `WalkPastMemoSkipsEveryRepeatedAliasTest` with the counters moving 4→8 tests and 4→0 skips; (C) the forward escape scan disabled (`dsscp` `85dd911c…`→`f1e55606…`) reds `MirEscape.LoadStoreAndGepContainASlotWhileACallArgumentPublishesIt`, `Rule3b_PhiMergingASlotAndAParameterIsUnknownAndEscapesTheSlot` and — the miscompile arm — the pass-tier CSE pin, which then reuses the PUBLISHED slot's reload, i.e. forwards a stale Load. Completeness is CHECKABLE rather than argued, to the standard P38 set: two sweeps over the WHOLE `MirOpcode` enum assert the use table's default arm is `Escapes` and that every value-numbering candidate has an operand-determined origin, and the pre-existing point-cover differential (`spec ⇒ production` over every ordered pair of program points) now runs with the index's OWN escape object threaded into the oracle — an oracle at a different precision is not an oracle. **⚠ ONE THEOREM MOVED AND IT IS RECORDED, NOT PAPERED OVER:** `mirAliasProbeSubstitutionPreservesClobberVerdict`'s equal-opcode + equal-TypeId + not-`Alloca` premise is a TYPE-level licence, and Rule 3b is not a type test — two `Gep`s of the same result type, one based on a non-escaped slot and one on a parameter, pass the three-argument predicate and have OPPOSITE Rule 3b verdicts (pinned, both polarities). | `D-OPT7-INLINE-FRAME-SENSITIVE-INTRINSIC` | P0 | ✅ CLOSED | **✅ CLOSED 2026-08-26 (P39 lane E) — the inliner now REFUSES what it cannot prove frame-safe, and the row's central PREMISE IS REFUTED: the hazard was never going to arrive as a registry-minted `IntrinsicCall`.** ★ WHAT WAS MEASURED, because the trigger as written ("the first frame-sensitive intrinsic is registered/emitted by a frontend") turns out to be unfirable as stated. (a) The C frontend NEVER registers or constructs an intrinsic: `cst_to_hir` contains zero references to `registerIntrinsic` or `HirKind::IntrinsicCall`, so the HIR intrinsic registry is empty through every real compile. (b) C DOES have intrinsics — 30 of them, declared as `builtinFunctions` in `c.lang.json` with a `lowering` verb (`umulh`, `bswap`, `popcount`, `clz`, `ctz`, the `stdc_*` family, the atomics, the complex accessors, `barrier`, `seh_exception_code`, `seh_exception_info`) — but EVERY ONE lowers through the closed `BuiltinLowering` enum to a DEDICATED MIR opcode, never to `MirOpcode::IntrinsicCall`. (c) The same is true of every frame-sensitive C construct: `va_start`/`va_arg`/`va_end` are first-class HIR nodes (`HirKind::VaStart`/`VaArg`/`VaEnd`) reaching dedicated MIR leaves, `setjmp` is an FFI `Call` carrying `MirInstFlags::ReturnsTwice`, VLA teardown is `StackSave`/`StackRestore`, and SEH is the five `Seh*` ops. (d) So DSS ALREADY HAS frame-sensitive intrinsics in the only sense that matters — `_exception_code()` / `_exception_info()` are 0-operand MIR value ops, and a 0-operand op takes nothing from the instruction stream, which makes the frame it executes in its ENTIRE meaning. Measured cost today: ZERO, since nothing emits one. An implementation firing on every lexed `#error` would turn all 49 into hard user errors and break EVERY macOS compile — strictly worse than the P0015 it replaced. **MECHANISM (agnostic; no engine identity branch):** two OPTIONAL `PreprocessConfig` words `errorDirective`/`warningDirective` (`readOptWord`, the `pragmaDirective`/`embedDirective`/`lineDirective` pattern — there is no `directives` array to extend), valued in `c-subset.lang.json`; two `else if` arms placed INSIDE `handleDirective`'s dispatch chain **below** the `if (!stackActive()) return end;` gate, which makes dead-branch silence structural rather than checked. The arms must NEVER move into the unconditional `#if`-family block above the gate (that block runs in dead regions on purpose, to keep `condStack_` balanced) — stated as an anti-instruction in the code. Two DISTINCT codes `P_PreprocessorErrorDirective`=0x001E / `P_PreprocessorWarningDirective`=0x001F, because `DiagnosticPolicy::suppress` keys on the CODE — one shared code would make `--suppress` of `#warning` noise also silence every `#error`. `emitPP` gained a defaulted trailing severity param (48 pre-existing call sites byte-unchanged: 51 `emitPP(` lines = 1 definition + 50 calls, minus the 2 new arms); `#warning` = Warning, and `hasErrors()`/`pp.fatal` were verified to let the build proceed through compile→link→run. Operand is a RAW source slice, never macro-expanded (gcc/clang parity); a bare `#error` with no operand is legal (`pp-tokens_opt`) and still fires. `P_PreprocessorErrorDirective` is the FIRST `P_*` member of `unsuppressable_codes` (all 127 prior entries are D_/F_/H_/I_/K_/L_/R_/A_/S_ (the table is 128 with this one)) — a user-authored abort must not be suppressible into a silently-built invalid configuration; a new tier line documents the family break. **★ HONEST NET EFFECT — do not misread the next corpus run:** all 49 `#error` sites are in LIVE branches (DSS predefines no `__GNUC__`/`__clang__`/`__x86_64__`/`__arm64__` — grep-verified 0), so this cycle **re-codes 49 P0015 → 49 P001E at the same 49 sites** rather than clearing them: 153 → ~152. That is the point — the old message was an actively misleading lie ("DSS lacks this directive") sent users hunting a missing feature instead of a genuinely-rejected configuration. **The only site this cycle actually CLEARS is the `#warning` at `sys/cdefs.h:81`** (live under `#if !defined(__GNUC__)`), and since nearly every Apple header includes `sys/cdefs.h`, dropping it from Error to Warning is the load-bearing half. ROOT CAUSE: the tokenizer splits a literal into a `StringStart` token holding ONLY the opening quote plus a COALESCED BODY token covering the bytes BETWEEN the quotes, so the closing quote belongs to NO token's span and a first..last `SourceSpan::join` stops one byte short. FIX: re-consume the trailing byte, GUARDED on it actually being `"` or `'` so a stray unpaired quote (`#error abc"`, already covered by its StringStart's own span) can never gain a phantom character. ★ WHY ALL 13 PINS MISSED IT: every one used BARE PROSE, and `"abc" tail` also passes because the join ends on `tail` — so the suite was green over a SUBSET of the operand FORMS while the single most important form was broken. This is the §A.5 multi-form trap verbatim: a multi-FORM contract needs a test per FORM, not per site. Reading the SQLite source settled it: the call sits in `#ifdef _WIN32 … #elif defined(__APPLE__) → sysctl(CTL_HW/HW_AVAILCPU) … #else → sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN) #endif`. **A real Apple toolchain never compiles that `#else` arm.** DSS reached it because `__APPLE__`/`__MACH__` appear NOWHERE in `src/dss-config/` — grep-verified. That cascade is the CORRECT direction — it is what a real Darwin compile does — and is measured by re-running the corpus. ═══ ★ GENERAL RULE: a target's **platform-announcement macros are part of its ABI contract**, not a nicety — omitting them does not disable platform code, it silently selects the WRONG platform code. Members (2) and (4) took shape (b); (1) and (3) took (a) because their keys are not enum-shaped. **Prefer (b) whenever the key set is a closed enum.** Shape (b) also deletes code rather than adding it: (4)'s re-key removed the raw-string lookup entirely, because ✔TREE **both** accessor call sites (`src/program/program.cpp:896`, `src/program/compile_pipeline.cpp:1434`) already held an `ObjectFormatKind` and were calling `objectFormatKindName()` purely to feed a lookup that could silently miss. ⭐⭐ **THE SEVERITY OF ONE INVALID VALUE IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE VALUE — IT IS A PROPERTY OF THE CONSUMER, and this is the most transferable finding of TF-C76.** The identical `"unknown"` sentinel is a silent NO-OP where the consumer treats `Unknown` as *absent* (five of the six sites: an extern library that never resolves, a macro predefined nowhere, a descriptor that matches no target), and a silent **MISCOMPILE** where the consumer treats `Unknown` as a *lookup key* — `elementCoreByFormat` stored a LIVE row under it and `resolveElementCore` matches a default-constructed `Unknown`, yielding a wrong `wchar_t` WIDTH. **So triaging a sentinel hole by inspecting the loader tells you nothing about its severity; you must read the consumer.** ★ **AND THE ENUMERATION METHOD, which is the reusable part: ENUMERATE BY GREPPING THE VALIDATING FUNCTION, NEVER FROM A REPORTED LIST.** TF-C76's six sites were found by grepping `objectFormatKindFromName` — not from the list it was handed, which is why it found sites nobody had named. [orig NEW c18, refined c19] A `//` line comment AFTER code on a line, IMMEDIATELY followed by a `#` directive on the next line, makes the preprocessor FAIL to recognize the directive: it leaks to the parser → `D0004 <malformed include>` + `P0001 expected 'IncludeKeyword' got 'define'`, then a full cascade. Precise repro (CLI-confirmed): `int a; // c\n#define Z 1\nint b=Z;` → P0001. A `//` comment ALONE on its line before a directive (`// c\n#define Z 1`) WORKS; a trailing `//` comment ON the directive line (`#define Z 1 // c`) WORKS; a `/* */` comment before a directive WORKS — only `<code> // comment` then a directive breaks. NOT silent (loud parse error). Likely root (confirm at fix time): `MacroExpander::firstOnLine` + the `//`-comment token swallowing its trailing newline, so the `#` after `code // comment` scans back through the comment (trivia, not-newline) to the code `;` and is judged not-first-on-line → not stripped as a directive. PRE-EXISTING (FC14-era `firstOnLine`; NOT introduced by c17/c18 — neither touched directive recognition). NOT on the SQLite path (sqlite3.c uses `/* */`, so the c18 re-probe did not hit it — IncludeKeyword count 0). The `#` IS first-on-line, so `firstOnLine` is not the gate. That case is already open as [[D-CONF-CORPUS-NO-DIRECTION-FOR-A-C23-REMOVED-CONSTRUCT]] and is NOT decided here. ✔**AND THE ALIAS IS MEASURED TO MEAN typeof_unqual, NOT MERELY TO LEX**, which a parse-only probe cannot see: under clang 19.1.1 `const int x = 1; __typeof_unqual__(x) y = 2; y = 3;` compiles clean while the identical program spelled `__typeof__(x)` fails *cannot assign to variable with const-qualified type*. ⚠ **AND THE DSS-SIDE DISCRIMINATOR IS DIFFERENT FROM THE REFERENCE-SIDE ONE — A MEASUREMENT THAT CHANGED THE WITNESS'S DESIGN.** ✔MEASURED at the pre-change HEAD: in DSS a `const`-sourced `typeof(g) x = 1; x = 2;` compiles CLEAN under EVERY spelling, because only `VolatileQual` is interned on a TypeId and const is carried by a separate declarator scan — so ASSIGNABILITY cannot tell the two arms apart here and an example built on it would have been VACUOUS. The channel that does discriminate is `_Generic` over a POINTER to the typeof result: `__typeof__(g) *p` selects the `volatile unsigned char *` arm and `__typeof_unqual__(g) *p` selects the plain `unsigned char *` arm. FIX (single file, agnostic, NOT §B): a new `declaratorObjectIsConst` helper (semantic_analyzer.cpp) — descend the per-slot declarator to its inner declaratorRule, and if it has ≥1 pointer layer, the object is const iff the LAST (outermost, source-order) pointer layer carries the const marker; with NO pointer layer the legacy whole-decl scan applies (scalar / typedef'd-pointer head const). Mirrors the c27 per-layer volatile walk in `declaratorDeclaredType`. Const stays a SYMBOL flag (NOT a type qualifier like c27's `VolatileQual`) because — UNLIKE volatile — const has no per-access codegen effect; the architect's Option-2 (a `ConstQual` lattice type) was rejected as a ~100-site surface buying nothing the helper doesn't. ★ CODEGEN NUANCE (the architect's "no codegen effect" claim was INCOMPLETE — caught + verified): `isConst` DOES thread to `MirGlobal.isConst` → `.rodata`/`.data` global placement (asm.cpp). So arm64's `popcount` row carries **NO `encoding` at all** (that IS the fact: AArch64 has no scalar-GPR population count) and a `lowering` block with two width-keyed sequences: `movq_gpr_to_xmm` → `popcount_bytes` → `addlanes_bytes` → `movq_xmm_to_gpr`. ★ **NO NEW VERB SET, NO NEW REGISTER CLASS, NO REGALLOC CHANGE — all three MEASURED, not asserted.** The two cross-class moves REUSE the shared verbs x86_64 already declares (`movq_gpr_to_xmm` / `movq_xmm_to_gpr`), which exist as two rows for the very reason arm64 needs two: the variant guard keys only on (operandKinds, width) and cannot tell the directions apart. Only the two genuinely-new operations got new vocabulary, and both are named by OPERATION and LANE ELEMENT rather than by ISA (`popcount_bytes`, `addlanes_bytes`) — an AVX-512 x86_64 declaring VPOPCNTB inherits the same sequence text. The temporaries are `fpr` (the D/S views), which AAPCS64 already makes allocatable, so the 128-bit `vr` class stays non-allocatable exactly as its register rows say and Lane I's allocator files were never touched: ✔MEASURED, the allocator assigned `d29` with zero changes to `lir_regalloc.*`. ★ **ENGINE CHANGE: TWO LINES, AND THEY CLOSED A GENERALITY GAP RATHER THAN A SPECIAL CASE.** `lowerPopcount` probed the mnemonic and then emitted ONE instruction of it, which silently assumes every realization is one instruction. It now routes through `lowerBitCountViaDeclaredRealization`, ONE owner shared by Popcount, Clz and Ctz (they were three copies differing only in the slot), which asks the target BOTH questions: does it name a realization, and does it spell that realization as one instruction or several. No CPU, mnemonic or lane arrangement is named anywhere in `src/`. ✔**MEASURED — EMITTED SHAPE FIRST, THEN RUNTIME ON REAL SILICON.** arm64-elf: the emitted body is `fmov s29,w16 / cnt v29.8b,v29.8b / addv b29,v29.8b / fmov w16,s29` and its 64-bit twin; **62 instructions → 14** across the two wrapper functions (a 4.4× reduction — the SWAR's 2 `mul`, 8 `and`, 8 `lsr`, 4 `add`, 2 `sub` all go to zero), and the program RUNS under qemu-aarch64 and exits with the hand-derived answer. ★★ **RUNTIME ON THE NATIVE aarch64 VPS (4-core), a 60M-iteration release-config benchmark, 5 runs each, every build exiting with the checksum `aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc -O2` computes for the same source: 580 ms → 226 ms, a **2.57× SPEEDUP** (before 579-582 ms, after 225-227 ms; `main()` 108 → 60 instructions). ⚠ **AND THE EMULATOR SAID THE OPPOSITE, WHICH IS WHY THE VPS WAS USED.** ✔MEASURED: under qemu the 14-instruction vector build timed SLOWER than the 62-instruction SWAR, because qemu translates every AdvSIMD instruction through a helper call. **A qemu wall clock is not an instrument for a SIMD-vs-scalar comparison** — sound for correctness, useless for this, and it would have been reported as a regression by anyone who trusted it. ★ The `gcc-13 -O2` control emits the IDENTICAL `cnt`/`addv`/`fmov` sequence, so the realization is the reference's own choice rather than an invention. Removing the row reproduces the pre-change lowering BYTE-IDENTICALLY (md5-equal artifacts), which is the third assertion that proves the mutant was read. ⚠ **THE HAND-DERIVED ENCODING WORDS WERE ALL SIX WRONG AND THE ASSEMBLER IS WHAT CAUGHT THEM** — `0x9E670000` had been converted to 2657419264, which is `0x9E650000`, i.e. FCVTAU. | `D-CSUBSET-ALLOCA-ADDRESS-REMATERIALIZE` | P0 | ✅ CLOSED | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-06-30 (p19 Cluster G c69; NOT §B) — a body-local alloca's ADDRESS is rematerialized at each use (a fresh `lea_frame_slot` per use) instead of held in one entry-spanning vreg.** ROOT (un-masked by the c69 entry-block alloca-hoist above): hoisting every alloca to entry makes its address-value live from entry; reusing ONE address vreg across that range tips a register-pressure cliff (`examples/c/index_negative`'s `main` takes addresses of locals → `R_SpilledDueToPressure` + `L_VirtualRegInPostRegalloc` scratch-pool exhaustion at the rewrite stage). The new `lea_frame_slot` virtual op is DISTINCT from `alloca` so the frame-layout slot-count scan is unchanged (exactly ONE slot per original alloca). A CONSTANT-offset Gep whose base IS an alloca (`&local[constIdx]`/`&s.field`) FOLDS its displacement into ONE sp-based `lea [sp + slotOff + disp]` (via an optional ImmInt operand on `lea_frame_slot`) — cheaper (one lea) AND load-bearing on arm64: without the fold, a >16 MiB `disp` in the un-folded `lea_frame_slot` base + `lea [base+disp]` pair lowers to the arm64 MOVZ/MOVK macro `ADD Xd,base,Xd` which clobbers `base` when regalloc coalesces the tiny-range remat base into the Gep result (base==Xd → SIGSEGV, `examples/c/large_frame_beyond_16mib` under the full-release-like pipeline); folding makes the base `sp` (never the result), so the macro is safe. Corpora `examples/c/index_negative` (→42; RED-ON-DISABLE → the scratch-pool exhaustion compile error) + `large_frame_beyond_16mib` (→42 on arm64-qemu; the const-disp fold is what keeps it green under remat). Verified RUN-green on all 3 legs (Win pe compile + WSL x86_64-elf + arm64-qemu). | | |

| `D-CSUBSET-VLA-FOR-INIT-SCOPE` | P2 | ✅ CLOSED | ✅ **LANDED 2026-07-14 (VLA C5) — a for-INIT VLA (`for (int a[n]; …; )`) now gets FULL for-scope block teardown.** (This anchor was briefly a fail-loud DEFERRAL earlier in this SAME cycle; the code-audit correctly flagged that gate as a REGRESSION — a top-level for-init VLA compiled + RAN pre-C5, function-scoped + epilogue-freed — and it contradicted the user OPTION-C full-general-teardown directive, so it was replaced with real teardown before the cycle closed. The prior "leaks per-iteration" rationale was factually wrong for a top-level for-init.) MECHANISM: a for-init VLA is declared ONCE at loop entry and PERSISTS across all iterations; C5 frees it ONLY on the loop-EXIT edges, NEVER on the back-edge (freeing it there = a use-after-free of `a[]` in iteration 2+). `emitStackSaveForVla` accepts a `ForStmt` scope node (single-declarator for-init: `hir.parent(declNode) == ForStmt`); the For driver captures the VLA watermark BEFORE the init (`f.vlaBase`), so the for-init frame sits at exactly `vlaBase` and the BODY block's per-iteration teardown (whose watermark is DEEPER, captured after the init) can never reach it (the depth bookkeeping keeps them distinct). The For driver emits ONE StackRestore at the loop EXIT block (the merge of the cond-false edge + every `break` — a break already restored the body VLAs to the post-init watermark, so both predecessors arrive with SP at the post-init level); `continue` frees only body VLAs (post-init watermark), keeping the for-init live; a `goto` OUT of the loop restores the for-init via the ancestry walk (`vlaFrameEnclosesLabel` treats a ForStmt scope as whole-for). Pins: `ForInitVlaEmitsForScopeTeardownAtLoopExitOnly` (for-init-only → 1 save + 1 restore, NONE on the back-edge) + `ForInitAndBodyVlaTornDownAtDistinctPoints` (for-init + body VLA → 2 restores in DIFFERENT blocks) + the `c99_vla_loop` phase-6 runtime witness (a for-init VLA in a 400000-iteration outer loop, written at k=0 + read at k>0 — catches BOTH a back-edge-free [use-after-free → wrong total] AND a leak [overflow]). Multi-declarator for-init VLAs remain deferred → `D-CSUBSET-VLA-FOR-INIT-MULTIDECL`. | | |

Apple clang 21.0.0: rc=0 plus a real warning `[-Wunknown-warning-option]`, fatal only under `-Werror`. MSVC 19.51.36252: `/wd2065` — a WELL-FORMED number naming a real diagnostic that `/wd` cannot silence, the closest analogue of the DSS question that exists anywhere — emits command-line warning `D9014` and CONTINUES. None hard-rejects the silencing form at parse time, so rejecting would have made DSS strictly harsher than all three on a flag whose whole purpose is to be script-driven, and would have broken shared CI scripts on an INTERNAL DSS reclassification (a code joining the closed table) with no change on the user's side. **The `--suppress=0xFFFF` precedent does NOT govern:** that reject refuses MALFORMED input naming NO diagnostic; this is WELL-FORMED input naming a REAL one, and refusing input that means nothing is a different decision from refusing input that means something the compiler declines to do. ★ gcc carries an asymmetry that settles the direction: it HARD-ERRORS on `-W<unknown>` (the ENABLING form, rc=1) while accepting `-Wno-<unknown>`. (c) ROW ORDER is part of the contract: every id-to-row lookup keeps the FIRST row, so alias rows append after the canonical one. Identity ranking: externally-visible over module-private, strong over weak, then lowest symbol id. Only ELF can produce it. This also REMOVED A PERMISSION THAT WAS HALF TRUE: the ELF overlap guard had waved equal-start pairs through 'because routing to either is offset-correct' — true of the offset, FALSE of the relocation. ⚠ SEVEN MUTANTS WATCHED, subject-binary mtime confirmed each time. REFERENCES: clang 18.1.3 accepts 297/297; gcc 13.3.0 accepts 279/297 and its only refusals are the 18 `_BitInt` probes, refused because gcc 13 has no `_BitInt` TYPE at all, not because it rejects the construct — so the union accepts every probe and the bar binds. ⚠ THE INVARIANT WAS RIGHT AND IS UNTOUCHED: relaxing the CondBr-expects-Bool check would have traded a loud refusal for a silent miscompile (branching on a raw enum word or a function's address); the conversion was owed by the front end. FIX (`src/hir/lowering/cst_to_hir.cpp`, three arms, each PROJECT-AND-RE-ENTER in the c91 Array arm's shape so there stays ONE construction of the truth test): Enum → `enumUnderlyingOrSelf` (the SAME owner `usualArithmeticCommonType` and `integerPromotedType` use) then the ONE `coerce` funnel then re-enter, which brings the C 6.3.1.1 integer promotion and the `Ne(_,0)` with it; FnSig → the existing `coerce` FnSig→Ptr decay funnel then re-enter onto the null-pointer arm; NullptrT → the Bool literal `false` directly, which KEEPS the `I_NullptrTypeInMir` tripwire true rather than weakening it. All three are UNGATED and read TypeKind SHAPE only — the semantic tier owns whether a language admits the conversion (`isAssignable`'s `scalarConvertsToBool` and `enumConvertsToArith`), this tier only REALIZES it, exactly as `coerce`'s Enum↔arith arm already states. The now-redundant enum bridge inside `coerce`'s `_Bool` arm is DELETED rather than left beside its replacement: two owners of the enum→int rule in one file is the shape that drifts. ⚠ NARROWER TRUE CLAIM RECORDED FOR NullptrT, because the first measurement conflated two defects: `if (nullptr)` — the LITERAL — always worked (it is an integer zero before the chokepoint sees it); only a NullptrT-typed VALUE was broken, and such a value today comes only from a `nullptr_t`-typed object whose initializing store is still refused one tier down. WITNESS: corpus `examples/c/scalar_condition_conversions` (16 arms over the six sites plus the `_Bool b = e` form, on an enum local, a wider-valued enum, an enum-typed bit-field, a function designator and `nullptr`; ⭐ every enumerator used as a truth value is EVEN and nonzero — EVEN=4, W_HIGH=256 — because the tempting wrong fix, a Cast-to-Bool that MIR lowers as Trunc, keeps only the LOW BIT and would call `if (EVEN)` false; the FALSE side of each site is scored too; exit 136, byte-equal to gcc and clang at -O0 and -O2; registered in BOTH runners) plus `HirLoweringC.EnumConditionTakesTheTruthinessChokepointAtEverySite` (7 enum→int truth tests, one per site) plus `HirLoweringC.FunctionDesignatorConditionDecaysAndTakesTheChokepoint` plus `HirLoweringC.NullptrTypedValueInAConditionBecomesTheBoolFalseLiteral` (HIR tier deliberately — see the narrower claim above) plus `MirLoweringC.ScalarFamilyConditionsLowerToABoolCondBr` (every CondBr's condition operand read off the terminators, ≥6 so it cannot go vacuous). A function-like macro is expanded only where its name is followed by `(` (C 6.10.3p10), so C 7.1.4p2 keeps the function addressable in as many words ("it is permitted to take the address of a library function even if it is also defined as a macro") — the import is LIVE. ✔**MEASURED by `nm -u` on the emitted object, gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 SEPARATELY, agreeing on every row**: under a function-like shadow `&amp;name`, `(name)(1)` and the bare designator all REACH THE SYMBOL while the plain call is eaten; under an object-like shadow all four are eaten. `#undef` frees BOTH forms and therefore discriminates nothing — excusing a shadowing on that basis would excuse every shadowing there is. ✔**The same table re-run against DSS itself reproduces all six rows**, so no preprocessor change was needed. ✔**Reproduced end-to-end through the CLI** on a `$DSS_CONFIG_ROOT` copy: pre-fix `dsscp` (md5 c6501b98) REFUSED both the function-like and the object-like shape at load; post-fix (3eb0e052) LOADS the function-like one with `&amp;name` undefined in the artifact and STILL REFUSES the object-like one. **THE FIX** — the discriminators are now the FORM *and* the REFERENCE, never the name: a defect is *object-like ∧ overlapping ∧ non-referencing*. `MacroBody` gained `functionLike`, read from `params` — **the same key `decodeShippedMacros` reads**, so the two cannot drift — and read **PER BODY**, because `decodeShippedMacros` refuses an entry carrying both a body key and `variants`, so a variants macro's `params` can only live on the variant and one arm may be function-like while its sibling is not. The diagnostic now names the form and offers `params` as remedy (a). ✔**Corpus re-measured**: 31 same-name (macro body × symbol row) pairs — 21 overlapping-and-referencing (tgmath), 10 non-referencing on disjoint formats (2 fn-like, 8 object-like), **0 refused before and 0 after** ⇒ the narrowing changed no in-tree verdict; it only stopped refusing a shape the corpus had not yet needed. **PROOF**: 8 pins in `test_shipped_lib_descriptor.cpp`, both arms; 3 REMOVE-direction mutants through ctest with 3 distinct verdict sets and a changed subject md5 in every arm (M1 delete the guard → the 3 refusal pins red, every accept pin green; M2 delete the function-like exemption → the 3 function-like accept pins red, refusals green; M3 read `params` off the ENTRY → exactly `MacroVariantEveryArmFunctionLikeIsAccepted` red). (ii) Sizing a read to the frame's exact remainder means a peer declaring `Content-Length: 4000000000` would have the buffer RESIZED to four gigabytes before one byte arrived — the old chunked read was accidentally immune because it only grew as bytes turned up. `kMaxReadStepBytes` (1 MiB) clamps the ask; clamping DOWN is always safe because fewer bytes than the frame owes are still bytes already promised, so the exactness property that fixes the blocking is untouched. ★ **This hole was found by re-reading the fix rather than by a test, and it is the reason the arm count is five: a fix that trades a hang for an allocation bomb has not landed.** ⚠ **PORTABILITY IS BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY PLATFORM FORK:** the contract chosen (`ByteSource::read` = "block until EXACTLY this many, or the stream ends") is the one `std::fread` can honour on BOTH Windows and POSIX; the POSIX-shaped "return whatever is available" is what stdio cannot portably give, and reaching for it is what would have needed an `#ifdef`. The `_setmode` binary-mode call moved OUT of the transport and INTO `StdinByteSource` / `StdoutByteSink`, so constructing a transport in a test no longer reconfigures the process's real standard streams. | (closed — P42 lane P) | `src/lsp/transport.cpp` · `src/lsp/transport.hpp` · `src/lsp/json_rpc.cpp` · `src/lsp/json_rpc.hpp`; pins in `tests/lsp/test_stdio_transport.cpp` and `tests/lsp/test_json_rpc.cpp`; with [[D-TEST-LSP-STDIO-TRANSPORT-DEFERRED-THE-ONLY-TESTS-THAT-COULD-CATCH-IT]] |

| `D-CSUBSET-C11-THREADS-TIMED` | P0 | ✅ CLOSED | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-09-01 (cycle P49, lanes `th` then `tw`) — `<threads.h>` is now COMPLETE on all three object formats, which is what `__STDC_NO_THREADS__` being defined NOWHERE has been promising since Cycle 2 (C11 6.10.8.3 / C23 6.10.9.3 make not defining that macro a promise of the whole header).** ⚠ **THE ROW'S ORIGINAL SCOPE WAS WRONG AND WAS CORRECTED BEFORE IT WAS CLOSED:** `mtx_timedlock`, `cnd_timedwait` and `thrd_equal` were not elf-FFI-only — they were ABSENT FROM EVERY FORMAT, and only `thrd_sleep` carried an elf entry, so four C11 functions were undeclared on every leg. ★ **THE PREREQUISITE THAT GATED THIS ROW WAS THE pe `struct timespec` LAYOUT, AND LANE `th`'s MEASUREMENT OF IT STANDS UNCHANGED:** `{long long tv_sec @0 (8B), long tv_nsec @8 (4B)}`, sizeof 16, `_Alignof` 8 — mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 (ucrt) and MSVC 19.51.36252 AGREEING, each probed SEPARATELY with a `_Static_assert` battery over `sizeof`/`offsetof`/`_Alignof` plus `_Generic`, each with a deliberately-false CONTROL arm that failed to compile — against glibc's 8-byte `tv_nsec`; and that measurement found a LIVE LATENT MISCOMPILE rather than merely an unverified number, in `time.json` AND `sys/stat.json`, both of which declared `timespec` FLAT `{i64,i64}` while listing `pe`, so every pe TU wrote 8 bytes into a 4-byte field — the same-size trap `struct timeval` already taught this project, since sizeof is 16 and tv_nsec sits at offset 8 on BOTH worlds. ★★ **LANE `tw` THEN SHIPPED THE RECIPES, AND FOUR OF THE PREMISES IT WAS HANDED WERE REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT.** (1) **The stated design was wrong about the CLOCK:** this row's closing cell said `GetTickCount64` supplies the deadline loop, but C11 states `mtx_timedlock`'s and `cnd_timedwait`'s deadlines as TIME_UTC CALENDAR times and `GetTickCount64` is a monotonic milliseconds-since-boot counter that cannot answer that question at all — the pe arms read `GetSystemTimeAsFileTime` and convert through the 11644473600-second FILETIME epoch offset, and `GetTickCount64` is not used by any recipe. (2) **`windows.json` did NOT already carry every primitive needed:** `GetThreadId` was absent and had to be added (✔MEASURED present in the live kernel32 export table at ordinal-table entry [820] by `objdump -p C:/Windows/System32/kernel32.dll` before being declared, per [[D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT]]), because pe's `thrd_t` IS a HANDLE while `thrd_current()` answers kernel32's PSEUDO-handle `(HANDLE)-2`, so a handle-value comparison reports NOT-EQUAL for the very thread asking — a wrong answer with no fault, and `GetThreadId` resolves the pseudo-handle exactly as MSVC's own `<threads.h>` does by comparing ids. (3) **`pthread_mutex_timedlock` IS ABSENT FROM DARWIN**, ✔MEASURED by LINK PROBE on macOS 26.6.2 / Apple clang 21.0.0 where every other primitive in the same battery (`pthread_cond_timedwait`, `pthread_cond_timedwait_relative_np`, `nanosleep`, `pthread_equal`, `clock_gettime`, `gettimeofday`, `mach_absolute_time`) LINKS and that one does not — so the macho arm is the SAME trylock/deadline loop as pe rather than a direct pass, and the loop is the implementation rather than a workaround because neither platform offers another construction. (4) **TWO EXPORT INSTRUMENTS LIED AND A THIRD ANSWERED HONESTLY:** `readelf --dyn-syms` TRUNCATES long names to `cnd_[...]@@GLIBC_2.34` and reported `mtx_timedlock` NOT FOUND on a libc that exports it, while `nm -gU`/`dyld_info` over `/usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib` report ZERO for every symbol on macOS 26 — including `_nanosleep`, which certainly exists — because that path is not a file on disk but a dyld-shared-cache entry; `nm -D --defined-only` and the LINKER are the instruments that do not lie here, and both elf legs were re-censused with the first (glibc 2.39, x86_64 under WSL and aarch64 on the native arm64 VPS: `thrd_equal@@GLIBC_2.28` T, `thrd_sleep@@GLIBC_2.28` **W** — a WEAK definition, which the eager-import law permits — `mtx_timedlock@@GLIBC_2.34` T, `cnd_timedwait@@GLIBC_2.34` T). ⓘ Two further findings are recorded where they were made rather than here: an `Arg` materialized AFTER a Call reads a parameter register the callee has clobbered (measured as an exit 10 from this cycle's own `thrd_equal` witness on its first run, now stated at the arm), and WSL2's CLOCK_REALTIME steps by +29 s and -27 s about every five seconds while CLOCK_MONOTONIC stays exact (✔REPRODUCED with a gcc-built control, 1100 ms for a 1100 ms nanosleep, 8 of 8) — which redesigned the corpus witness rather than being worked around. | **SHIPPED — `thrd_sleep`, `mtx_timedlock`, `cnd_timedwait` and `thrd_equal` each carry a TRIPLE entry in `threads.json` (elf plain FFI + pe `synthesize` + macho `synthesize`), the four recipe ids joined the closed vocabulary in `src/ffi/shipped_lib_descriptor.cpp` (threads family 21 → 25, total 27 → 31), and eight new arms landed in `src/mir/merge/synth_threads_shim.cpp` — four per vehicle.** ★ **THE pe ARMS:** `thrd_sleep` reads `tv_sec` as 8 bytes at offset 0 and `tv_nsec` as **FOUR** at offset 8, converts with the sub-millisecond remainder rounded UP (`Sleep` has millisecond resolution and never returns early, so rounding up is what makes "at least the requested interval" true; mingw-w64's own `thrd_sleep` truncates and can sleep short) and pays it out in a LOOP capped at 0xFFFFFFFE per iteration — the cap is not decoration, since a duration whose low 32 millisecond bits landed on 0xFFFFFFFF would hand `Sleep` the INFINITE sentinel and hang the thread forever; `mtx_timedlock` is a `TryEnterCriticalSection`/`GetSystemTimeAsFileTime` deadline loop with a 1 ms nap (Win32 has no timed critical-section acquire, and switching `mtx_t` to a kernel Mutex object would buy one and LOSE `cnd_wait`, which requires a CRITICAL_SECTION for `SleepConditionVariableCS`); `cnd_timedwait` is a SINGLE block over `SleepConditionVariableCS` with the absolute deadline converted to a relative millisecond timeout clamped to [0, 0xFFFFFFFE] and the verdict computed branchlessly as `(1 - succeeded) * (2 + 2*isTimeout)` from `GetLastError() == ERROR_TIMEOUT (1460)`, because that call returns 0 for BOTH a timeout and a real failure and collapsing them would report a programming error as a timeout; `thrd_equal` compares `GetThreadId` of each handle. ★ **THE macho ARMS:** `thrd_sleep` is a DIRECT pass to `nanosleep` (same timespec in, same optional remainder out, same 0/-1 convention as C11's "interrupted by a signal"); `cnd_timedwait` a DIRECT pass to `pthread_cond_timedwait`, which takes the same absolute TIME_UTC timespec, with the errno mapped (`ETIMEDOUT` is 60 on Darwin — errno.json's own macho arm, ✔re-measured by a RUN probe on the host, and the same mapping glibc's `cnd_timedwait` performs); `thrd_equal` a DIRECT pass to `pthread_equal`, which needs no pseudo-handle indirection because `thrd_current()` on this vehicle is already a real `pthread_self()` id; `mtx_timedlock` the deadline loop, over `pthread_mutex_trylock` + `clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME)` + a 1 ms `nanosleep`, reading `tv_nsec` as EIGHT bytes (Darwin is LP64 — ✔MEASURED by a RUN probe: sizeof 16, tv_sec@0/8, tv_nsec@8/8, `_Alignof` 8, `sizeof(long)` 8; CLOCK_REALTIME is 0 and ETIMEDOUT 60, both PRINTED by a compiled program rather than read off a man page). ✔**THE WITNESSES RUN, THEY DO NOT MERELY COMPILE, AND THEY RAN ON ALL FOUR LEGS.** `examples/c/c11_threads_timed` pins each function FROM BOTH SIDES — `mtx_timedlock` must refuse an already-expired deadline on a mutex another thread holds AND wait on one that thread is about to release; `cnd_timedwait` must refuse an expired deadline AND wake when signalled — so a constant `thrd_timedout` passes one arm and fails the other, and it POISONS every `struct timespec` to 0xFF before assigning, because a cleanly-zeroed struct hides an 8-byte read of a 4-byte field behind zero pad. `examples/c/c11_thrd_equal` makes a spawned thread compare its own `thrd_current()` against the `thrd_t` its creator holds, published through a mutex main owns from before the thread exists, so nothing depends on timing. Both reach BOTH example runners. with a RECURSIVE attr it returned at once. **The failure is a HANG, not a wrong value** — it compiles, links, loads and then stops, which is why no compile-only pin could ever have seen it. ★★ **AND IT WAS BELOW THE UNION, WHICH IS WHAT MADE IT A DEFECT RATHER THAN A CHOICE.** C11 7.26.4.2 / C23 7.28.4.2 make `mtx_plain \| mtx_recursive` a mutex the owning thread MAY re-lock, and BOTH other implementations that ship `<threads.h>` honour it — ✔MEASURED, each probed SEPARATELY, by a program that re-locks on a child thread with a 2 s bounded parent wait: glibc 2.39 through **gcc 13.3.0** and again through **clang 18.1.3** (relock proceeds for type 1 AND for type 3), and **MSVC 19.51.36252**'s own `<threads.h>` (`.../VC/Tools/MSVC/14.51.36231/include/threads.h`, same result). ⓘ mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 ships NO `<threads.h>` and is therefore not a reference on this question — checked on the filesystem, not assumed. ⚠⚠ **THE GATE'S OWN TRIGGER WAS SPENT AND THE ROW'S STATED OBSTACLE WAS FALSE.** The trigger read "`thrd_create` (Cycle 2, makes it observable)"; The cause was ONE decision in `constIntExpr`: it passed no float-literal token set and no `allowFloat`, on the reading that an integer-required consumer must refuse a float ANYWHERE in the expression (the comment called it "the F3 wall"). The existing keys are all keyed by REFERENCE KIND (`externCallDispatch` for calls, `dataImportBinding` for data reads, `externAddrBinding` for address materialization); this one is keyed by the SYMBOL's binding, in the SAME agnostic `SymbolBinding` vocabulary `ExternImport.binding` and `ModuleSymbol.binding` already speak, so the next format needing the distinction DECLARES it rather than having a second mechanism invented. And the axis is structural, not stylistic: a pc-relative code relocation can only name a target that will have a SECTION and an address, a WEAK undefined may legally resolve to NOTHING (COFF spells that as an ABSOLUTE value-0 symbol), and a GLOBAL undefined has no such resolution — the link finds a definition or fails loud. `weak` IS the set of bindings whose references cannot be direct there. ★★ THE RULE HAS EXACTLY ONE OWNER: `ObjectFormatSchema::externRefTakesImportSlot(SymbolBinding)` — dispatch + narrowing + the unnarrowed default, written once. The linker's `materializeObjectImportSlots` calls it per import; MIR→LIR is threaded the DECLARED list and reads the ANSWER out of ONE per-symbol set. `externRefSlotBindings()` returns the same answer as a set, DERIVED from the predicate and PROJECTED over `kSymbolBindingTable`, never re-decided and never retyped. ★★★ AND THE SECOND HALF IS WHAT MAKES IT SAFE, WHICH IS PRECISELY WHAT `wf` WAS RIGHT TO WORRY ABOUT: `lowerCall` used to read the FORMAT-level dispatch while the address arm read a per-symbol set. Narrowing only the linker would leave a strong import's `FF 15` dereferencing its own address — so the call site moved onto the SAME set (`externRefUsesSlot`), and so did the F128-softcall and atomics-runtime call sites, and both SELF-SERVE MINTS now enter that set on the ctor's rule. One shape per symbol, decided once, and the two tiers cannot disagree. NOT NARROWED: `dataImportBinding` — its unconditional slot has an INDEPENDENT measured reason (`ld` refuses a direct rel32 against a symbol it must AUTO-IMPORT from a DLL), so the binding axis does not govern it. FAIL-LOUD: four load-time refusals (a narrowing without `indirect-slot`; an EMPTY list, which cancels rather than narrows; `local`, which no import can carry; an unknown or duplicate spelling) plus a NEW MIR→LIR ctor arm — a NARROWED format emits BOTH shapes, so it needs the plain `call` opcode as well as `call_indirect_via_extern`. ✔MEASURED AFTER, each consumer probed SEPARATELY on the SAME DSS object, BEFORE from a pristine `0cbf3b62` CLI built by `git archive` into the scratchpad and read against its own config root. WEAK object, unchanged in every cell: `.text` `REL32 .refptr.maybe` ×2, `FF 15`, one `.rdata` ADDR64 COMDAT; link.exe 14.51 rc 0 RUN 42 and RUN 40 with a definition, mingw GNU ld 2.42 rc 0 RUN 42 / 40, lld-link 18.1.3 rc 0 RUN 42 / 40. (2) ✔MEASURED, the substitution is MEANING-PRESERVING — same effective address, same access size, same register — so it is an encoding election, not the emission of a different instruction, which is what this cell's ⚠ was really guarding against. That is the whole cost, and it is bounded by the meaning-preservation measurement above. ★★★ **HOW, AND IT IS TWO CONFIG KEYS THAT ARE ONE MECHANISM — NEITHER IS SAFE ALONE.** (a) `guard.immMultipleOf` (new, `TargetEncodingVariant`): the DIVISIBILITY axis, the third member of the family `immMin`/`immMax` and `negValue` already form. `immMin`/`immMax` bound an INTERVAL; a `imm12.scaled` slot encodes `byteOffset/accessSize` and carries only the MULTIPLES inside one, so a range-only guard MATCHES an offset its own encoder then REFUSES — and because election commits to an opcode, the fallback is never reached. All 18 scaled variants of `load_u`/`store_u`/`fldr_u`/`fstr_u` now declare `immMin: 0`, `immMax: 4095×accessSize` and (where the size exceeds 1) `immMultipleOf: accessSize`, mirroring exactly what their slot can carry. (b) `opcodesAreRankedEncodings` (new, `AsmInstructionSpelling`): states that a row's `opcodes` are ENCODINGS OF ONE OPERATION, ranked, so `electOpcode` settles a tie by rank instead of refusing it as ambiguous. The default REFUSAL is unchanged and right for every other row — it assumes a tie means the dialect cannot say which INSTRUCTION was written, which is true of different instructions and false of two encodings of one. `ldr` is now `["load_u","fldr_u","load","fldur"]` and `str` `["store_u","fstr_u","store","fstur"]`; **`ldur`/`stur` still name ONLY the unscaled opcodes**, which is what keeps the one-directional asymmetry the references have. ⚠ THE RANK CHOOSES ONLY AMONG CANDIDATES THAT ALL FIT: a candidate is reached only after its own guard accepted the operands, so order can never select a form that cannot carry the value. ★★ **THE `ldur` REACH DOES NOT LEAK, WHICH IS THE FENCE THIS CELL NAMED.** An offset outside both reaches is still refused, pinned at every width and in both directions by `AnOffsetOutsideBothReachesIsStillRefused`. ★★ **DIAGNOSTIC QUALITY IS PRESERVED AND IN ONE PLACE IMPROVED.** The per-width *not a multiple of the N-byte access size* message is no longer reachable from `.s` — because that input now COMPILES, so there is no refusal left to keep specific. | `D-PP-SINGLE-PASS-INCLUDE-RESOLUTION` | P1 | ✅ CLOSED | **✅ CLOSED 2026-09-03 (P57 lane pp) — the include PRE-SCAN's macro state IS the authoritative `MacroExpander` now, hosted as an ORACLE, so there is no second evaluator left to drift.** The row's residual reproduced EXACTLY as written. ✔MEASURED at fcb3a9d7 through the shipped CLI: `#define ENABLED(x) (x)` + `#if ENABLED(1)` gating `#include "feature.h"` was REFUSED with `P_PreprocessorIncludeError` ("… is LIVE here but the include pre-scan could not evaluate its conditional guard"), no artifact. ★★ **REFERENCES, EACH PROBED SEPARATELY 2026-09-03 — the union is UNANIMOUS, so this was never a vote to weigh:** WSL gcc 13.3.0, WSL clang 18.1.3 and mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 each COMPILE AND RUN the construct (exit 0 / 42), and MSVC 19.51.36252 accepts it (`cl /nologo /c /std:c17`, exit 0 — a front-end question needs no vcvars). ⚠ MSVC must be probed from PowerShell: Git Bash rewrites `/nologo` and `/c` into paths and the run silently links instead of compiling. ★★★ **THREE THINGS IN THE ROW WERE REFUTED, and the third is why this closed in a lane instead of a plan.** (1) "re-implements conditional evaluation" was WIDER THAN THE TREE — ✔MEASURED by reading the file at fcb3a9d7, `CondFrame`, `sbStackActive`, all four `sbHandle*` transitions, the ICE `evaluateIfExpression` and the `defined` barrier `PpIfOperandBarrier` were ALREADY single-impl and ALREADY driven by both passes; the duplication was exactly ONE thing, the MACRO EXPANSION callback (`sbExpand`, object-like-only) and the `SbMacro` table feeding it. CORPUS: `examples/c/per_member_packed` (the whole-composite twin is `examples/c/packed_struct`, which is this row's standing CONTROL — it must stay green under every per-member mutant). Builds ON P56's [[D-CSUBSET-TRAILING-ATTRIBUTE-RUN-IS-READ-AT-THE-WRONG-GRANULARITY]]: its `AttrAppertainment` axis ALREADY gave the right grain (`structMemberAttrList` is `declarator`, which for a struct field IS per-member), so no fifth axis value was invented and the per-declarator `attrFacts` copy gets the prefix and suffix positions right at once. Roots in TF-C73's `structMemberAttrList`, whose `$packedStaysNoneComment` argued the member position was safe because *"one attribute does not mean two things depending on which side of the declarator it is written"* — sound for every other name in the table and false for `packed`, which is why that position dropped it in silence for cycles; THAT sentence is the one this row retires. Interacts with TF-C82 / [[D-PP-PRAGMA-REGISTRY]] (`maxFieldAlign` is the per-COMPOSITE dual, and its reintern carry was MISSING and is fixed here, pinned by `PackCapSurvivesReintern`) and with TF-C97 / [[D-CSUBSET-PACKED-BITFIELD-INTERACTION]] (whose ONE-clamp refactor is what made this a per-field INPUT rather than a second algorithm; its straddle refusal is the named residue this row inherits and pins AS a refusal). Also [[D-CSUBSET-MEMBER-ALIGNAS]] (the RAISE-only per-field channel, which cannot express a lowering — `max(natural,1)` is a no-op on every field this attribute is written on, which is why a separate channel was required) and [[D-CSUBSET-COMPOSITE-ALIGNED]] (the whole-composite raise, which still composes: `{char a; int z <pk>;} aligned(16)` is 16/16/z@1). Landed alongside lane `al`'s [[D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS-TYPEDEF-PARAM-PARSE]] in two of the same files; `al`'s versions were taken from the MAIN tree and byte-verified before the first edit, so neither closure can revert the other. SP+outgoingArgAreaSize)` and every dynamic object is lifted above it — so a captured stack **watermark** means `SP + outgoingArgAreaSize`. The `sp_copy` capture gains `add dst, bias` and the C5 `sp_restore` gains `sub SP, bias`, **both pinned by a data dependence rather than by emission order**. ── ⚠⚠ **THE ROW WAS TOO WIDE IN TWO WAYS AND BOTH ARE REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT.** (1) Its central claim — *"no correct base choice in the fixed-reservation model"* — is **FALSE**. The ABI needs the args at `[SP+0..)` **only AT THE CALL**, and SP is exactly the register the runtime `sub` keeps current. **What has to move is the VLA OBJECT, not the args.** (2) Its scope sentence said *"calling convention 'ms_x64'"*; ✔MEASURED, the refusal fired identically on **`sysv_amd64` and `aapcs64`** — the row named ms_x64 because that is where it was measured, not because it was the only one. ── ✔**THE pe64 PLACEMENT ORACLE AGREES WITH DSS BYTE FOR BYTE.** mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0, for a VLA function calling a **10-argument** callee: `sub $0x78,%rsp ; mov x26, sp ; add x26, x26, #0x20`, and for the restore `mov sp, x27 ; sub sp, sp, #0x20`. ── ✔**REFERENCES, each probed SEPARATELY, binaries EXECUTED** (VLA object + call, expected 30): gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3, aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 under qemu, and mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 native pe64 all compile and RUN to **30**; Discrimination chain, in order: (1) a SQL-level probe on the arm64 DSS shell was CORRECT — bigint `ORDER BY` properly ascending AND `SELECT random() AS y FROM t1 ORDER BY 1` came back SORTED; (2) a TCL probe showed the list sqlite returned had **0 descents** (i.e. genuinely sorted) and it was `lsort -command bigintcompare` that reordered it; (3) `bigintcompare` is `expr {$a-$b}`, which OVERFLOWS int64 on the extremes (−9.2e18 − 3.3e18 ≈ −1.25e19) and so exercises Tcl's bignum promotion — a path living entirely in gcc-built `libtcl8.6.a`; (4) **decisive**: a PURE gcc `tclsh8.6` with ZERO DSS code linked showed `expr {9223372036854775807 + 1}` = `-9223372036854775808` (wrapped) on arm64 vs the correct `9223372036854775808` on the x86_64 system tclsh, while explicit `entier(1)<<70` was correct in both (so libtommath was fine — only AUTOMATIC overflow promotion was broken). ROOT: the original `build_tcl.sh` passed `--host=aarch64-linux-gnu --build=x86_64-linux-gnu`, which makes autoconf treat the build as CROSS and **skip every `AC_RUN_IFELSE` probe**, taking hand-fed cache answers instead (`tcl_cv_type_64bit='long int'`, `tcl_cv_strtod_buggy=ok`, `tcl_cv_strtod_unbroken=ok`, `ac_cv_func_strtod=yes`). | `D-TEST-EXAMPLES-RUNNER-PARALLEL-CONTENTION-FLAKE` | P3 | ✅ CLOSED | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-07-24 (TF-C58 gate — trigger FIRED: it red-ed 3 of 4 consecutive full Win ctest runs, a different example each time). ROOT CAUSE FOUND, and it is NOT the spawn-timeout fragility this row hypothesized.** The real mechanism is a `ScratchDir` PATH COLLISION (`tests/test_support/scratch_dir.hpp`, shared by every test that needs a scratch dir). The ctor built `<base>/<pid>-<counter>` and called `create_directories`, checking only `ec` and IGNORING the return value — and `create_directories` reports SUCCESS when the directory ALREADY EXISTS. The dtor's `remove_all` swallowed its `ec`, so directories leak whenever a spawned example binary still holds a handle or a run is killed (**55** were sitting in `test-scratch/examples/` when this was found). A process drawing a recycled PID (Windows reuses them freely) plus the same counter value therefore SILENTLY SHARED a stale directory, and the runner's next `copy_file` — which does not pass `overwrite_existing` — threw `filesystem error: cannot copy file: File exists [.../main.c]`. That explains every observed symptom the timeout theory could not: it hits a DIFFERENT example each run, it reproduces in SERIAL runs too (`-j1`, via PID reuse against leaked dirs, not concurrency), it passes on isolated re-run, and it worsens the longer a working tree goes without cleaning `test-scratch/`. **FIX (one chokepoint — both runners and every other ScratchDir consumer inherit it):** the ctor now LOOPS on `create_directory` (singular) and accepts only a slot whose creation it actually won, which is atomic in the OS and therefore race-free across concurrent `ctest -j` processes as well as stale-dir-safe; a bounded attempt cap fails loud naming the accumulation; and the dtor now WARNS on stderr instead of silently swallowing a failed `remove_all`, so leakage is visible while still small. WITNESS: `test_scratch_dir.cpp::StaleDirectoryOnTheNextSlotIsNotReused` plants a populated directory on the exact slot the ctor will draw next (predicted from a probe ScratchDir's own filename, so it pins real ctor behaviour) — **red-on-disable DEMONSTRATED: restoring the return-value-ignoring `create_directories` fails BOTH expectations, while the pre-existing `MultipleScratchDirsGetDistinctPaths` stays GREEN** (it advances the counter either way — an inert pin that was green through the entire lifetime of the bug, the §A.5 trap). Post-fix: full Win ctest green. ★ NOTE the spawn-timeout hypothesis recorded below was never confirmed; if example flakes recur after this, re-open on that theory with fresh evidence rather than assuming it. **_(Original entry retained below.)_** ⏳ was OPEN, trigger-gated -- named 2026-07-23 (TF-C54 gate; recurring since >=TF-C51).** Under a PARALLEL full `ctest -j4` on the Windows leg, examples-runner entries (each spawns a compiled example subprocess with a 5s timeout) intermittently FAIL on load-timing -- distinct entries each occurrence (TF-C51: 2; the TF-C54 iterations: `deep_expr_lower`, then `bare_int_condition`, then 4-at-once right after a WSL-gate teardown), EVERY one passing on an ISOLATED re-run, and the same tree 727/727 on the WSL leg. NOT a product defect (the examples are EXEC-path front-end/codegen witnesses; the flaking set is uncorrelated with the diff under test) -- a HARNESS timing fragility: subprocess spawn + 5s wall-clock timeout under heavy parallel load. Operational protocol (memory + skill): run the Win ctest ALONE (never concurrent with a WSL gate) + re-run any examples fail ISOLATED to discriminate flake-vs-regression. This row makes the recurring pattern REGISTRY-VISIBLE (§A.7) instead of per-cycle folklore. Trigger: a CI leg (which runs examples serially today) starts hitting it, OR the local flake rate materially disrupts gates. Closing work: make the runner robust under parallel load -- e.g. a load-scaled/generous spawn timeout, ctest RESOURCE_LOCK/serialization for examples entries, or a retry-once-with-loud-tag arm (design choice at closure; a silent auto-retry that could mask a REAL intermittent regression is NOT acceptable per §A.4). | Make examples-runner ctest entries robust under parallel load (today: run alone + isolated re-run protocol). | `tests/examples/examples_runner.cpp` + `integrated_tests/runner.cpp` (the two runners); [[D-EXAMPLES-RUNNER-CLI-SUBPROCESS-NESTED-DEPENDSON]] (where the 5s-timeout masking bit before); the dss-cycle/memory operational protocol; ★ **2026-08-04 POINTER ADDED — the "run alone (never concurrent with a WSL gate)" protocol quoted in this row is SUPERSEDED and must not be re-derived from here:** it was refuted by measurement at TF-C105 (concurrent Windows ctest + WSL gate + agents rebuilding `build-dbg` → 771/771, exit 0) and the surviving, mechanism-specific rule is [[D-GATE-SHARED-DLL-RELINK-UNDER-RUNNING-CTEST]] — concurrency is fine, relinking the shared DLL underneath a running ctest is not |

FIRST corpus example `examples/c-subset/staticlib_resolve_roundtrip`: `dsslib.c` (exporting `dss_lib_answer`) built as a STATIC library (a `.lib` on pe64 / a `.a` on elf64 via the c171-D `-staticlib` format), `main.c` (extern `dss_lib_answer`) RESOLVED against it -> the c169/c170 COFF (or c165 ELF) static-link pulls the member into a SELF-CONTAINED exec -> exit 42. ADDITIVE: `dependsOn` defaults empty -> every pre-c171 example is byte-identical. — ORIGINAL (c162): ⏳ trigger-gated. MEASURED: BSD sed extracts **0** lines with `\?` vs **52** with the POSIX form; GNU sed extracts **52 either way** — so the fix `\(local \)*` (`\(...\)` + `*` are both core POSIX BRE, no `-E`, no dialect dependency) leaves the Linux/Windows legs BYTE-UNCHANGED. `*` still matches the `local`-prefixed form, preserving the deliberate extract-then-fail-at-runtime design of the sibling anchor. **(2) `bash` resolved via PATH, not the running interpreter (the root cause).** `build-and-test.sh` re-execs itself into bash 4+ (line 67), then invoked the self-test as a bare `bash "$_selftest"` — PATH bash on macOS is **/bin/bash 3.2**, which has no `declare -A`. Same bug at `test-confound-scope.sh` running its generated temp script, where bash 3.2 parses re-emitted `declare -p` associative-array output arithmetically (`host: unbound variable`). MEASURED under 3.2: **all 20 assertions failed on a CORRECT classifier**. (2) measurement: with stdin an OPEN PIPE never written and never closed (the strongest simulation of a blocking console), an aborted fixture exits rc=1 in 8.8 s, 0 survivors — same as NUL stdin; ~25 abort runs left 0 zombies. The real PID was simply a HEALTHY run 1h12m into a legitimate ~2.5 h `all` tier, with `corpus.log` at 79 MB and still growing. ★ OPERATOR ERROR, named so it is not repeated: the second run was launched by the operator who KNEW a detached `all` run was in flight (had even noted its result would not count) and did not check whether it had finished before starting another. Concurrency hazards do not announce themselves — check for a live run before starting one. | Fixed. Side benefit: single-instance makes process-killing safe by construction (anything running OUR fixture path is by definition a leftover). ★ OPEN SUB-DECISION: the `.ps1` derives `$Work` from the repo root with NO override, so two concurrent Windows runs are now REFUSED outright (the `.sh` has `OUT_DIR`). The capture was correct and was pointed at a stream already emptied one level down. `cl`'s silencer is removed; `call vcvars` keeps its own, because on success it prints a pure-noise banner and its failure is already covered upstream by `locateMsvcToolchain`. ⓘ **THAT ORDERING IS THE LESSON:** part (1) alone would have shipped looking finished, and its output — the honest string "NO output at all" — would have been read as "the compiler said nothing", which is false. Only running the failure arm distinguished them. ✔**DEMONSTRATED END-TO-END:** with a deliberate syntax error injected into the emitted `probe.c`, the message now carries `probe.c(3): error C2018: character 'U+40' is not permitted here` and eight more lines, file and line included; mutation reverted byte-identical (sha256) and both ABI witnesses re-run green. ⚠ **THE RISK IS SHELL QUOTING AND IT IS LOUD, NOT SILENT:** get it wrong and the build fails on every host and every run — checked on Windows (cmd.exe) and under WSL (POSIX sh) both. That is the opposite of the failure mode this file warns about, where a wrong redirection SILENTLY became "no compiler installed". ★ **THE ONE-SHOT FAILURE THAT EXPOSED THIS IS A SEPARATE, STILL-OPEN QUESTION — see [[D-TEST-NATIVE-PROBE-COMPILE-FAILS-UNDER-CONCURRENT-LOAD]].** This row closes the DIAGNOSTIC gap only; it does not explain the failure, and must not be read as having done so. | Cross-refs: `tests/core/native_c_probe.hpp` (`captureCmd`, `tailOf`, and the capture at the CompileFailed arm) · `tests/core/test_packed_abi_conformance.cpp` (the witness that hit it) · [[D-TEST-FIXED-SCRATCH-PATH-POPULATION]] (ruled OUT as the cause here: `ScratchDir` claims its directory atomically with `create_directory`, so a collision is excluded by construction) | |

| `D-GATE-ANCHOR-GUARD-FAILS-OPEN-ON-MISSING-ROOT` | P3 | ✅ CLOSED | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-03 (TF-C112) — ★★ THE GUARD THAT ENFORCES THIS REGISTRY COULD REPORT SUCCESS WHILE CHECKING NOTHING, AND THE BUG WAS INTRODUCED BY THE COMMIT THAT WIDENED IT.** Found by an independent code review of TF-C111. `scripts/check-anchor-registry/check-anchor-registry.sh` collected anchors as `{ grep …; grep …; } \| sort -u \|\| true` under `set -euo pipefail`; that `\|\| true` swallowed BOTH greps' exit status alongside their stderr (`2>/dev/null`). ✔Consequences, traced: **(a)** rename or move ONE scan root and it drops out SILENTLY — the reported count falls and the guard still says OK, so the `real-examples/` coverage TF-C111 had just added could be un-added by an unrelated refactor with nothing to notice; **(b)** if EVERY root failed, `SRC_ANCHORS` is the empty string, the `while` loop's single blank iteration is skipped by its own `[[ -z ]]` guard, `MISSING` stays empty, and the script prints **`anchor-registry: OK (1 src anchors all resolve to plans)`** — the "1" being `echo "" \| wc -l` — and exits **0**. ★ **A guard reporting SUCCESS while verifying NOTHING is the worst defect a guard can have**, and it is the precise silent-failure class this registry exists to prevent; the file's own comment already named *"the silent no-op version of this fix"* as the hazard while shipping exactly that. **FIX — two independent defences, deliberately both:** every scan root is asserted to EXIST before scanning (missing root ⇒ loud `exit 2`), and a **count FLOOR** (`ANCHOR_FLOOR=100`, far below the live 800 so ordinary churn never trips it) catches the present-but-unreadable case the existence check cannot. ⓘ The floor is necessary rather than belt-and-braces: `grep` legitimately exits 1 on "no match", so its STATUS cannot distinguish "clean tree" from "collapsed scan" — which is why simply deleting the `\|\| true` is NOT the fix. The real mechanism is a WITHIN-FAMILY VERSION GAP that gate cannot see — clang-18 reports `__STDC_VERSION__ 202311L` under `-std=c23`, so it is ENTITLED to judge every `@min-stdc 202311` probe, then refuses three of them in its own words (`unknown type name 'constexpr'`; `binary integer literals are a GNU extension`; `must specify at least one argument for '...'`), all three of which clang-19 accepts (positive control `a_bitint_c23`, accepted by both). Those rows read "a reference accepts" with clang-19 present and "NO reference compiler accepts" without it — a manufactured direction-B (13 to 15) plus 3 CORPUS-DISAGREES — and `a_va_opt_c23` additionally read STALE ACKNOWLEDGEMENT because DSS and the one entitled-but-stale oracle both said no, which `classify()` scored as AGREEMENT. That "now AGREE" was true of the two verdicts compared and false as an inference; NOT a second defect. | **DONE — the decision is split in two in `tests/conformance/test_reference_conformance.cpp`.** (1) `pin(expectRef, dssAccepted)` takes NO roster argument at all, so host-independence is a property of the SIGNATURE rather than a promise in a comment; it drives every DSS-facing red (direction A/B, unacknowledged divergence, stale acknowledgement). The descriptors, target register files, object formats, optimizer pipelines and language grammars all live in that tree ⇒ a packaged compiler could not resolve a single `#include <stdio.h>`. | **FIXED — three halves, one owner each.** **(1) THE INSTALL SET** — new `cmake/DssInstall.cmake` (self-contained module, one `include()` at the tail of the top-level `CMakeLists.txt`, deliberately conflict-free against `origin/main`'s mid-file additions): `install(TARGETS)` for the CLI + shared lib with a relocatable `INSTALL_RPATH` (`$ORIGIN`/`@loader_path`), the GNU-on-Windows runtime DLLs (whose list keeps its ONE owner in `src/CMakeLists.txt`, published as a cache variable rather than re-derived), and `install(DIRECTORY src/dss-config/)` **WHOLE** — a hand-listed subset would be a second owner of what the tree contains and would silently omit the next directory added. **(2) THE LOOKUP ARM** — precedence is now `$DSS_CONFIG_ROOT` → **INSTALLED LAYOUT (relative to the running executable)** → cwd walk. ★ **THE INSTALLED ARM OUTRANKS THE WALK, and that ordering is the safety property**: a packaged compiler must use the config it was installed with, never whichever `src/dss-config/` happens to sit in the ancestry of the directory a user stands in. It is INERT for development (a binary in `build/bin/dss/` has no installed data dir beside it), so nothing about the repo workflow moved. Once the installed root exists it is AUTHORITATIVE — a miss inside it STOPS the search rather than falling through, because mixing two config trees in one compilation is a silent wrongness of its own. The relative hop is **COMPUTED BY CMAKE** from the same `GNUInstallDirs` variables the `install()` rules use and forwarded as `DSS_INSTALL_CONFIG_RELDIR` (`#error` if absent), so the install set and the lookup cannot disagree about where the tree lives; an absolute `CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR`/`DATADIR` is a configure-time `FATAL_ERROR` because it would make the package non-relocatable. Executable path comes from the KERNEL (`GetModuleFileNameW`/`_NSGetExecutablePath`/`/proc/self/exe`), NEVER `argv[0]`. A not-found now LISTS EVERY PATH TRIED. ⚠ **ONE STATED NARROWING, recorded so it is not rediscovered as a bug:** the DIRECTORY form returns `std::optional`, so a skewed tree and a genuine miss are the same answer there — the skew EXPLANATION comes from the file form, which every compilation reaches first (the driver resolves the language schema before any directory lookup). Widening that signature would ripple into four files owned by concurrent work, and correctness holds either way because both forms run the SAME precedence, so a skewed tree is never USED and the two can never read different trees. **(3) SKEW FAILS LOUD** — the installed path carries the binary's OWN version segment (`share/dss-code-prime/<version>/dss-config`, gcc's `/usr/lib/gcc/<triple>/<ver>/` answer), so on that arm skew is **UNREPRESENTABLE** rather than merely detectable — a newer binary dropped over an older install fails loud instead of silently compiling against old descriptors; the two repo-shaped arms read the tree's own `VERSION` and REFUSE a mismatch naming both versions and the tree. ⚠ **RC'S BUILD STAMP WAS DELIBERATELY *NOT* REUSED, and its own header says why**: the stamp is maximally sensitive BY DESIGN (commit + dirty-content digest) because a cache key must over-invalidate, whereas a compatibility check must be exactly as sensitive as the compatibility boundary — reusing it would red every dirty dev build; its docblock also forbids a second includer, and `config_path_walk.cpp` lives in `core`, which would rebuild the world on every keystroke. **Both root on the SAME single owner** (the repo-root `VERSION` file), so this is one fact with two derived uses, not two owners. **VERIFIED — 4-mutant red-on-disable, five fail-closed clauses PLUS the mirror, every transition carrying an artifact-hash witness** (a PE relink changes the image even for identical source, so *changed* is the criterion, never *restored-to-baseline*): (A) the installed arm never resolves → RED; (B) the arm block MOVED below the cwd walk — a block move, so the ORDER claim is isolated from the EXISTENCE claim → RED; (C) the skew refusal removed → RED; (D) `install(DIRECTORY)` deleted → RED. ★★ **THE RED-ON-DISABLE CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT IN THE FIX ITSELF, and it is this cycle's lesson**: mutant A first came back **GREEN over a live mutant** because `installedConfigRootFrom` read the `DSS_INSTALL_CONFIG_RELDIR` macro DIRECTLY while the accessor `installedConfigRelDir()` read it separately — **two readers of one fact**, and the round-trip unit pin composed its expected path through the accessor, so the test was proving something about a path the implementation did not use. Collapsed to one reader; the mutant then went red. **Closing test — `install_scratch_prefix_smoke`** (a bare `add_test`, NOT `dss_add_test`, because the latter sets `DSS_CONFIG_ROOT` and the test would then measure the override): installs to a scratch prefix under the system temp dir and compiles **and RUNS** a hello-world (`#include <stdio.h>`, exit 42, asserted stdout). ★★★ **THE SOURCE TREE BEING OUT OF REACH IS ENFORCED, NOT HOPED**: every ancestor of the scratch cwd is asserted free of `src/dss-config` **to the filesystem root** (further than the resolver's 8-hop bound), `DSS_CONFIG_ROOT` is unset and re-asserted, and — the measurement rather than the argument — **THREE NEGATIVE CONTROLS**: with the installed tree renamed away the same compile MUST fail (if it did not, the green run was reading config from somewhere else) and MUST list the paths it tried; with a FULL COPY of the config tree planted in the cwd ancestry carrying a foreign `VERSION` the installed tree must still win (an EMPTY decoy would prove nothing — the probe would miss it either way); and that same tree named through `DSS_CONFIG_ROOT` must be REFUSED as skew naming both versions. The installed-vs-source file comparison is a **TOTAL set comparison against `src/dss-config/`**, never a list written in the test — ✔the first draft DID hand-list files and named one that exists only in a work-in-progress tree. Same total comparison guards the release leg in `pipeline-pkg.yml` (which now stages `cmake --install` and tars the PREFIX TREE, since `DSS_BUILD_TESTS=OFF` there means the ctest entry does not run). ⚠ **THE WARM `dist/release/` CACHE IS DELIBERATELY *NOT* INSTALLED AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN SILENT**: ✔MEASURED that the content-hashed object cache did not exist when this landed, so nothing produces `dist/` and an `install(DIRECTORY)` aimed at it would create an empty destination and report success — the vacuous-fix shape, reading for months as though the warm cache were shipping. (2) **A lock on the remote build tree**: a second leg REFUSES (`exit 4`) naming the owner instead of destroying the tree; a lock whose owning pid is gone is stale and may be taken, so a killed leg cannot wedge the carriage.
